Ph.D. in Statistical Science (sunset)
Ph.D. in Statistical Science (sunset)
This degree program was merged with Luddy in 2026 and is now being offered as the Ph.D. in Informatics, Statistics Track.
Degree Requirements
Course Requirements:
A total of 90 credit hours, including at least 60 credit hours of coursework; dissertation research to reach 90 credit hours.
Core courses (9 credit hours):
MATH-M 413: Introduction to Analysis I
STAT-S 610: Introduction to Statistical Computing
STAT-S 611: Applied Statistical Computing
Data Analysis courses (10 credit hours):
STAT-S 631: Applied Linear Models I
STAT-S 632: Applied Linear Models II
STAT-S 690: Statistical Consulting
Advanced Statistical Theory courses (12 credit hours):
STAT-S 721: Advanced Statistical Theory I
STAT-S 722: Advanced Statistical Theory II
plus at least two semesters of
STAT-S 785: Seminar on Statistical Theory
Research Project (3 credit hours):
STAT-S 799: Research in Statistics
Elective and Minor courses (26 credit hours):
All students must complete a Ph.D. minor in another graduate program. Minor requirements are specified by the awarding department and are described in the University Graduate School Bulletin. All elective and minor courses must be approved by the Director of Graduate Studies.
Qualifying Examination:
Students must pass a qualifying examination on Statistical Theory, and complete a 1-semester research project under faculty supervision.
Dissertation:
A dissertation is required. The dissertation represents original methodological research by the student. The research should be of sufficient quality to merit publication in peer-reviewed journals.
Director of Graduate Studies
Fangzheng Xie
Associate Professor / Director of Graduate Studies
Email:
fxie@iu.edu
Website:
https://fangzheng-xie.github.io/
Dr. Xie's research interests include High-dimensional statistics, Network analysis, Bayesian statistics, and Computer models.
